newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank plans capital increase, profit up.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank plans capital increase, profit up.

text.p: Generale Bank NV, Belgium's biggest bank, said on Tuesday it was planning a 15 billion Belgian franc ($484 million) capital increase.
"The capital increase is neccessary to increase our flexibility and solvency," chief executive officer Ferdinand Chaffart told a news conference.
"It will make it possible for us to both take advantage of the acceleration in economic growth in those countries where we are active, and to continue to pursue our strategy," he added.
Generale Bank also reported an 8.6 percent rise in first-half 1996 group net profit to 7.31 billion francs from 6.73 billion in the year-earlier period.
The result was at the low end of analysts' forecasts.
Chaffart said he expected second-half 1996 earnings to be in line with those of the first half.
The capital issue had been expected following Generale Bank's acquisition last year of Credit Lyonnais Bank Nederland -- the Netherlands' fourth-biggest bank.
On the basis of the share price on September 9, the issue -- in the proportion of one new share for ten existing ones -- will be worth about 15 billion Belgian francs.
The issue will run from September 19 to October 4 and will be priced on September 18.
Chaffart said the issue price would be based on the bank's share price between September 10 and 18, minus a discount of seven to 12 percent.
Chaffart said the bank had no single specific purpose for the capital increase.
But he said, reiterating earlier statements, that Generale Bank is still interested in acquiring a bank in the German state of North-Rhine-Westphalia.

He added that, as far as priority activities are concerned, the bank is continuing to develop asset management, private banking and financial markets to diversify its income and offset pressure on interest margins. ($1=30.98 Belgian Franc)
